QF.id: AIFM CIII Modern Portfolio Theory and Capital Market Theory_15

question.text: Mr. Rahul Sharma, risk officer at Vindhya Event-Driven Fund, is explaining CML vs SML to the compliance team. Which of the following distinctions is CORRECT?

answer.text: CML plots expected return vs beta; SML plots expected return vs total risk (std dev).
Both CML and SML plot expected return vs beta, but with different intercepts.
CML applies only to individual securities; SML applies only to fully-diversified portfolios.
CML plots expected return vs total risk (std dev) and applies only to efficient portfolios; SML plots expected return vs beta and applies to ALL securities and portfolios.

explanation.text: The Logic: The Capital Market Line (CML) has total risk (sigma) on the x-axis and applies only to efficient portfolios combining the risk-free asset with the market portfolio. The Security Market Line (SML) has beta (systematic risk) on the x-axis and applies to ALL securities and portfolios — efficient or not — at equilibrium. The Trap: (A) inverts the axes. (B) ignores the axis difference. (C) inverts the scope of the two lines. Note: Workbook pages 61-66 cover CML, CAPM, and SML directly. Page 224 supports alpha as return over CAPM expected return, but stick to the axis/scope distinction when answering this question.
